title: You Set The Standard
paragraphs: I have a word, king. The word king, first and foremost, means ruler. Did any of you grow up with... those little plastic rulers in your bag when going to school? Or the wooden ruler? Do you remember the wooden ruler? They call them rulers, don't they? You take them to school, and they call them rulers. Well, they call it a ruler because the word ruler means standard. Have you noticed what the ruler does? It draws a straight line. What does a line do once it's drawn? Two things. First, he separates.

If you have a blank page with no lines, there is no chapter. The moment you draw a line, the separation occurs. Secondly, when you draw a line, you are setting a standard. This is what the word ruler or ruler means. The governor draws the line. God draws the line. He decides what is right or wrong, what is up or down, what is left or right. He decides what is good or bad. You don't decide that. God is the ruler. He is the one who draws the line. That is why God gave Moses a ruler.

When people were making mistakes and being corrupt, God gave Moses a ruler. He gave him 10 marks on the ruler. We call them the Ten Commandments. This is the ruler. This is the standard. O Moses, if they want to live properly, they must adhere to these standards. This is what the ruler means. So, the king means setting the standard.
